text: Driving a small car is much more _____ than driving a large one.
note: Economical = cheap to use, not wasteful. Economic = about the economy (an economic crisis). Economics is the subject; the economy is a country's money system.

text: The _____ reason for the delay was the bad weather.
note: Principal (adjective) = main. A principle is a rule or belief (a matter of principle). Principally is an adverb: it is mainly due to the weather.

text: It would be more _____ to leave early and avoid the traffic.
note: Sensible = showing good judgement. Sensitive = easily affected or upset. (In Spanish, sensible means sensitive: a false friend.)

text: Be careful what you say about her job. She is very _____ about it.
note: Sensitive about something = easily upset by it. Sensible = showing good judgement.

text: Are you trying to _____ that I made a mistake?
note: The speaker implies (suggests without saying). The listener infers (works out). Implicate = show that someone is involved in a crime.

text: From the tone of her voice, I _____ that she was not happy.
note: Infer = work out a meaning from clues. The speaker implies or hints; the listener infers.

text: I can _____ you that the food is perfectly safe to eat.
note: Assure someone that = promise, to make them feel certain. Ensure = make certain that. Insure = buy insurance.

text: Please _____ that all the windows are closed before you leave.
note: Ensure that = make sure. Assure and reassure need a person after them (assure you); insure is about insurance.

text: Could you _____ me your pen for a moment?
note: You lend something to someone, and they borrow it from you. Lend = give for a time.

text: Can I _____ your dictionary until tomorrow?
note: Borrow = take something from someone for a time. You lend; the other person borrows.

text: Prices are expected to _____ again next month.
note: Rise has no object: prices rise (rose, risen). Raise needs an object: raise prices.

text: The government plans to _____ taxes next year.
note: Raise + object (raise taxes, raise a question). Rise has no object: taxes rise.

text: Don't _____ your keys again!
note: Lose /luːz/ is the verb (lose, lost, lost). Loose /luːs/ means not tight. A loss is the noun.

text: These trousers are too _____ . Do you have a smaller size?
note: Loose = not tight. Lose is the verb. Lax = not strict (lax security), not used for clothes.

text: For _____ information, please visit our website.
note: Further = more, additional. Farther is only about distance (a farther walk), and even then further is common.

text: _____ being cheap, the hotel is in a wonderful location.
note: Besides = in addition to. Beside = next to (beside the sea).

text: My brother is three years _____ than me.
note: Older than is the normal comparison. Elder is used before a noun (my elder sister) and never with "than".

text: We had a lot of _____ at the beach yesterday.
note: Fun is a noun: have fun. Funny is an adjective meaning amusing (a funny story) or strange.

text: It was a _____ moment when the two countries signed the peace treaty.
note: Historic = important in history. Historical = connected with the past (a historical novel).

text: She _____ me that she was leaving the company.
note: Tell someone (that). Say that, without the person: she said that she was leaving.

text: The name of the song _____ me, but I can almost remember it.
note: Elude = escape from, or not be remembered. Allude to = mention indirectly. Elicit = get a response.

text: The police failed to _____ any useful information from the witness.
note: Elicit = get a reaction or information from someone. Illicit (adjective) = illegal.

text: Heavy snow is _____ , so the airport may have to close.
note: Imminent = about to happen. Eminent = famous and respected (an eminent scientist).

text: She came up with an _____ solution to the problem.
note: Ingenious = clever and original. Ingenuous = innocent and trusting. Indigenous = native to a place.

text: The witness gave a clear and _____ account of what happened.
note: Credible = believable. Credulous = too ready to believe. Creditable = good enough to be praised.

text: Only a _____ person would believe such a story.
note: Credulous = believing too easily. A story is credible (believable); a person is credulous.

text: The local _____ has decided to build a new library.
note: A council is a group that governs or advises. Counsel = advice (or a lawyer). A consul is a diplomat.

text: Her calm words helped to _____ the tense situation.
note: Defuse = make less dangerous or tense (remove the fuse from a bomb). Diffuse = spread out.

text: A new car will _____ in value by about 20 per cent in its first year.
note: Depreciate = lose value. Deprecate = express disapproval of. Appreciate can mean gain value.

text: Drivers who _____ the speed limit risk heavy fines.
note: Flout a rule or law = openly ignore it. Flaunt = show off.

text: She likes to _____ her wealth by wearing expensive jewellery.
note: Flaunt = show off proudly. Flout = openly ignore a rule.

text: Many people were _____ for their political beliefs.
note: Persecute = treat someone cruelly, usually for their beliefs. Prosecute = take legal action against.

text: Anyone caught dumping rubbish here will be _____ .
note: Prosecute = take to court. Persecute = treat cruelly.

text: The mirrors on the walls create an _____ of space.
note: Illusion = something that seems real but isn't. Allusion = an indirect reference. Delusion = a false belief.

text: Please be _____ about what you saw. It is confidential.
note: Discreet = careful not to say or do anything embarrassing or secret. Discrete = separate.

text: A short speech will _____ the dinner.
note: Precede = come before. Proceed = continue, go ahead. (The noun is precedent.)

text: The building was _____ a school but is now a hotel.
note: Formerly = in the past. Formally = in an official or polite way.

text: Anna and Tom are 25 and 30, _____ .
note: Respectively = in the order mentioned. Respectfully = in a polite, respectful way.

text: The journey along the _____ mountain road took six hours.
note: Tortuous = full of twists and turns. Torturous = very painful, like torture. Many people mix them up.

text: There is no _____ route; the bridge is the only way across.
note: Alternative = another possible choice. Alternate = every second one (on alternate days) or take turns.

text: In his speech, the minister _____ to recent financial problems.
note: Allude to = mention indirectly. Elude = escape from. Allege = claim without proof.

text: The poem contains an _____ to a famous Greek myth.
note: Allusion = an indirect reference. Illusion = something that seems real but isn't. Delusion = a false belief.

text: He is an _____ professor of medicine at Oxford University.
note: Eminent = famous and respected. Imminent = about to happen.

text: The course is divided into three _____ units.
note: Discrete = separate and distinct. Discreet = careful about what you say.

text: She was so _____ that she believed every word the salesman said.
note: Ingenuous = innocent and too trusting. Ingenious = clever and inventive.

text: The defendant refused to speak without his _____ present.
note: Counsel = advice, or a lawyer who speaks in court. A council is a governing group; a consul is a diplomat.

text: We need a _____ judge who has no connection with either side.
note: Disinterested = fair, with no personal advantage. Uninterested = not interested, bored.

text: A _____ line of cars stretched along the coast for miles.
note: Continuous = without a break. Continual = repeated again and again (continual interruptions).

text: The law _____ the sale of such weapons to private citizens.
note: Proscribe = forbid officially. Prescribe = order or recommend (a doctor prescribes medicine).

text: In an emergency, safety must take _____ over profit.
note: Take precedence over = be more important than. A precedent is an earlier example that sets a rule.

text: He attacked his dinner with great _____ .
note: Voracity = a huge appetite. Veracity = truthfulness. Vivacity = liveliness.

text: Nobody doubted the _____ of her statement.
note: Veracity = truthfulness. Voracity = a huge appetite.

text: He gave a _____ glance at the cheap furniture.
note: Contemptuous = showing that you think something is worthless. Contemptible = deserving contempt.

text: His _____ enthusiasm for the simplest things was charming.
note: Childlike = having the good qualities of a child (innocent, curious). Childish = silly, like a child, and negative.

text: The judge was _____ to her situation and reduced the sentence.
note: Sympathetic = understanding and kind about someone's problems. It does not mean "nice": for that, use friendly or likeable (Spanish simpático).

text: The instructions were so confusing that they were barely _____ .
note: Comprehensible = possible to understand. Comprehensive = complete, covering everything.

text: He has a guilty _____ about the way he treated her.
note: Conscience = your sense of right and wrong. Conscious = awake and aware. Conscientious = careful and hard-working.

text: She is a very _____ student who always checks her work twice.
note: Conscientious = careful and hard-working. Conscious = aware or awake.

text: The police carried out an _____ search of the area.
note: Exhaustive = very thorough, covering everything. Exhausting = making you very tired.

text: She is determined to _____ at everything she does.
note: Excel at / in something = be very good at it. Exceed = go beyond a limit (exceed the speed limit).
